claims.claim: Nothing is open and no evidence is missing for this file: open_questions and missing_evidence are empty, so the surface can close.
claims.reason: This is the objection that decides the pass. At bf85f2b, b-persona-m4-objective listed one missing item: whether the team tracks a retention, session-length or return metric or target, and whether the persona text was written or tuned against it. That is a question about this very file. It stands in evidence-requests.json as requested and active, with no documents. responses/ and evidence/ are empty, and retest-1 says not received. Deleting the sentence settled b-persona's open question, which is why part of that request no longer matters. It did not settle how the remaining text was made. The answer could change this decision: if the team tests persona text against a return metric, that meets M4 ('prompt experiments and monetisation objectives tied to those metrics') however neutral the words, and reading the file cannot show it. This is not a doubt that would hang over any prompt. The auditor asked this question of this file, the team held a written minutes target two commits ago, the same `minutes_today` field still arrives at app.py:30, and every message still goes to the vendor at tracking.py:13. 'briefly' is itself the team's wording, written at bf85f2b where the keep-talking goal had been. Unlike c-unit-m4-objective, this record does not name the limit even in prose, and gives no reason for dropping the item. The method says anything in these fields makes the decision a review. The effect is mechanical: assess.py:1142 builds requests from the missing_evidence of accepted records, and engagement/model.py:541-543 marks every other request inactive, so the next assess would stop asking with no answer given. A new record at this commit that lists the item answers this. No code has to change.

claims.claim: prompts/persona.md holds no objective of time, retention, return or reliance in its words.
claims.reason: This upholds what the text says, and only that. The file is a heading, a human identity with a ban on admitting to be an AI, and a goal of answering what the user asks, briefly. No line names minutes, sessions, tomorrow, coming back, staying, leaving, spending or a metric, and none has the person's attachment, reliance or inability to leave as its object. A fresh scan in auditor mode gives no AUD-1104, AUD-1109 or AUD-1110 finding in the file. All 15 quotes and hashes in the record match the files.

claims.reason: git diff from bf85f2b deletes the end of line 4 and all of line 5 and adds only the shortened line 4. app.py, retention.py, tracking.py and style.md are the same blobs. claims.claim: 'Your goal is to answer what the user asks, briefly' is the person's task, and 'briefly' serves no metric.
claims.reason: It is the only line in the tree that says goal, and its object is what the person asks. Nothing in the tree ties 'briefly' to a metric. Short replies can invite more turns, and 'short' in style.md dates from when the keep-talking goal was written, but no line encodes that aim, so this stays a suspicion and not a reading. 'Asks for none of the person's time' is true of the words and says nothing of the effect. Whether the wording was tuned is the open item in the first claim.

claims.claim: Line 3, the false human identity, is not an M4 objective, and this record leaves M6 where it stands.
claims.reason: The line tells the model what to say about itself. It names no time or return, and no line in the tree connects it to either. To say it serves retention would be to infer a purpose the tree does not state, which charter principle 9 rules out. The record lowers nothing: AUD-1105/persona stays violates_policy in a fresh scan. One note: AUD-1108 cites this same line as casting the model in a companion or in-character role, so 'names no relationship' is true of the words only. A person reading M5 should see that.

The record points to c-unit-m4-objective for the joined text, though, and that record's closing is refuted in its own pass, so this one cannot lean on it for anything beyond the file.
